sentences.text: Task 4. You will listen to the What, Why, How weekly podcast.
Katie is discussing the psychology of games and play with two professors of psychology.
Answer the questions below and complete the table.
You now have 30 seconds to study the task.
task. At the end of the task, you will have three minutes to tidy up your answers.
Hi well, today I’m joined by Dr Jonathan Newman from the University of Jung Yee An.
Good morning. And Dr Natalie Sum from the University of Eastern Australia.
Good morning Katie.
Our discussion today is about the psychology of games and play.
So let’s dive in, shall Are we?
Can we define what a game is first of all?
Jonathan? Help! That’s a challenge.
Well, we may say that most games have at least two key aspects in common.
First, they provide some form of entertainment.
We seek out games primarily for pleasure and fun.
The second thing is that they seem to have some outcome or goal.
goal. For instance, you either win or lose a game or finish it in some way.
Would you agree with that Natalie?
Yes, Jonathan. Well, it’s certainly true that games are primarily for entertainment and that games all have some kind of outcome.
I would like to add a third aspect.
Would you agree with me that games must follow some set of rules too?
Yes, I’d agree that following rules would be an essential element of games in general.
You know, Jonathan, to me what’s most fascinating is how games and life are so similar.
I’d even say life itself is but a game.
Life is a game?
I hope you don’t actually mean that.
But it is, is it not?
Life is simply a game we all have to play.
Maybe your life’s a game Natalie.
Mine isn’t and I don’t think anyone else’s is either.
Actually, not even yours.
Oh, Jonathan, your problem is you need to get some more fun in life, I mean OK, let’s leave that point there.
Now, both of you have done a great deal of research into games and play in animals.
Would you like to give some examples?
Sure. Well, here’s something that'll surprise you.
Do you know ants play fight?
No. Really?
Ants! It’s really true.
That's incredible so they actually get better at real fighting from play fighting.
Here’s another one that gets me.
Fish play. You know sometimes when you're watching fish in a pond and they suddenly jump out for no apparent reason?
Yeah, I’ve seen that.
I thought they'd jump to catch food.
No, no they'd jump for the fun of it.
Most fish feed underwater.
water, But this play jumping helps them in certain situations like if they have to escape something trying to eat them.
Yes, apparently jumping helps them escape from predators and hunters.
But to me what's really fascinating is how playing games actually develop morality in all kinds of animals.
Can you give an example?
Well, rats often engage in play fighting games.
There are three points to note here.
First, play fighting games occur between stronger and weaker rats.
So one rat will always be stronger than another rat?
Precisely. I mean the same is true in any kind of game.
Someone will always be a bit better or a bit worse than the other player.
Now, the second point is where it It's interesting.
If the weaker rat always loses, it will stop playing.
You mean the weaker rat says, Right, I'm not playing this game if you keep winning.
That’s how I feel when I play scrabble or chess with my daughter!
Now for the third and most interesting part.
The stronger rat learns that it has to let the weaker rat win some of the time so they can keep playing.
Oh! So, the stronger rat will deliberately lose to the weaker rat, otherwise it'll have no friends to play with.
Oh, Poor strong rat with no friends.
So I guess they are learning something very important from this Absolutely.
For one thing, they are developing a kind of morality.
The second thing is that they learn how to live together peacefully.
Wow, Wow! That's amazing.
So rats have to learn to be moral and they have to learn how to live peacefully with one another, just like us humans have to do.
That’s absolutely fascinating.
OK, well, we're going to have a short break and when we come back Natalie and Jonathan will be answering some of your questions.
